name: Roque de los Muchachos Observatory
aliases: Observatorio del Roque de los Muchachos

operator.value: Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (host observatory); CTAO-North hosted here per CTAO's own site listing
operator.quote: La Palma, Spain, and Paranal, Chile
operator.note: CTAO's own page names La Palma, Spain as one of its two array sites without naming a local operator sentence; the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias is the well-known operator of the wider Roque de los Muchachos Observatory but that specific operator statement was not seen in a source fetched this session.

intervals.label: hosts gamma-ray telescopes
intervals.quote: started operations in its final configuration in October 2003
intervals.note: Start date is a lower bound taken from MAGIC-I's October 2003 operational start (the earliest sourced gamma-ray-telescope activity at this site found this session), not a founding date for the wider Roque de los Muchachos Observatory itself, which predates both MAGIC and CTAO.

summary.plain: A mountaintop observatory on the Spanish Canary Island of La Palma that hosts several gamma-ray telescopes, including MAGIC and the northern half of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory.
summary.technical: Astronomical observatory on the island of La Palma, Canary Islands, Spain, hosting the MAGIC telescopes and CTAO-North (the northern array of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory).

notes: site_ids, accelerator_ids, beamline_ids, institution_id, document_ids, experiment_ids are deliberately not written (v0.2 A1 derived fields).

This facility is shared: created once by the cosmic-gamma workstream (owner of both experiment:ctao and experiment:magic per the wave-3 id registry), referenced by both experiment:ctao's facility_roles and experiment:magic's facility_roles. No other workstream should create a duplicate.

No founding/intervals data for the wider Roque de los Muchachos Observatory (which predates both MAGIC and CTAO) was sourced this session; intervals is left empty rather than guessed, and status 'active' reflects that both hosted experiments are currently operating.
